newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar/mark nearing big payday.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar/mark nearing big payday.

text.p: The dollar's steady advance above 1.76 marks on Tuesday brought it to within a stone's throw of its biggest technical plum in six years, analysts said.
Should the greenback take out the 1.7686 marks high from February 1994, it would open a channel to a test 1.8350, a level last seen in August 1991, chartists said.

"That would be an outrageously bullish signal and would lead to a retest of the February 1989 high at 204.70, though not in a straight line," said Joe Klettner, foreign exchange technician at Chase Securities Inc.
Dollar/mark could face minor mixed technical signals in the short-term, but chartists recommend bargain-hunting for what could be a spectacular ride.
"I'd be a buyer of dips rather than a seller, big picture. It's too close to (1.7686 marks) not to go up there and test it," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.
The dollar faces some declining daily indicators, even as longer-term oscillators are rising, suggesting sideways trade above 1.74 marks is possible for a week or so, Johnson said.
Klettner cites support at 1.7440 marks as a key level preventing near-term consolidation.
Mark/yen is teetering at critical support just below 64 that protects about four yen to the downside, chartists said.
A break there would be good news for dollar/mark, but would likely push dollar/yen back toward its 1997 low at 110.62, a level posted last month, analysts said.
"I expect 63.80 (mark/yen) to hold. If it does, I don't think we'll test that (dollar/yen) low," said Klettner.
Technicians see good support at 112 yen, which held for a time in June before finally giving way to the 110.62 low.
"If by Wednesday's close we're still above 112, you buy the smashdown to 112 with a stop below 111.60," said Johnson.
"As long as it closes Thursday above 112, we'll see a decent rally above 113, toward 114 or 115," Johnson added.
Sterling/mark's rally continues to bolster the dollar. Late Tuesday, the pound stood at 2.9730 marks, a key level that could, if held on a weekly closing basis, open a path to 3.04, Johnson said.
But the failure of mark/Swiss to advance with dollar/Swiss and dollar/mark offers a troubling sign for dollar bulls.
"That means the dollar is not as healthy as it appears to be and we'll have to be a little more respectful of the supports," Klettner said. --Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664
